newsitem.title: DENMARK: Foreign buyers help Danish bonds up in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buyers help Danish bonds up in quiet trade.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose in a quiet market on Friday with foreign buyers helping to fuel activity ahead of the afternoon's U.S. May unemployment and non-farm rolls data.
"It seems that foreign investors are being attracted to the Danish bond market as a safe haven during the ongoing EMU unrest. The U.S. employment data is awaited with interest," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.31 point up from Wednesday's close at 111.30, yielding 6.28 percent in turnover of 1.3 billion crowns.

The forthcoming seven pct 2007 benchmark was 0.40 point up at 103.88, yielding 6.46 percent in two billion crown turnover, while the 2006's June future rose 0.16 point to 111.16 with 1,699 contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.25 point to 89.55. The crown traded at 3.8076 per mark at 1130 GMT, virtually unchanged since the opening.
The 2006's 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one point to 47 bps while the 2007-bund differential had narrowed two bps to 65 by early afternoon.
